subject: ACTION: 600 North Speed Limit during construction
comment: Team, I am writing as a resident of 600 North to express serious concerns about the ongoing safety issues in our neighborhood due to the current construction and the unchanged speed limit of 35 mph through the work zone. With only a single lane available during construction, it has become extremely difficult and dangerous for residents—myself included—to safely exit our driveways. Vehicles often speed through the construction zone with little regard for those trying to navigate the area cautiously. There have already been several near-misses and accidents due to the lack of clear regulation and enforcement. I respectfully urge the city to immediately reduce the speed limit to 25 mph in the construction zone to protect both workers and residents. In addition, we request increased police presence to monitor traffic and enforce safe driving through the affected area. I would also like to report that the electronic sign asking drivers to merge into a single lane—which was placed in front of our home at approximately 1104 West—was hit by a vehicle two weeks ago and nearly destroyed. Thankfully, no one was injured, but this incident highlights the dangerous conditions we're currently facing. We appreciate the work being done to improve infrastructure in our area, but the current traffic situation is unsustainable and unsafe. Immediate action is needed before someone gets seriously hurt. Thank you for your attention to this urgent matter. Sincerely, Ted Dumont

subject: Mayor's proposed parking increase in the new budget
comment: Hello. I just saw a story that stated the Mayor's proposed budget would raise meter parking rates from 2.25 an hour to 3.50 an hour, a 55% increase!! And increase the hours to 10 pm. I work with Salt Lake Brewing Co., which owns and operates Squatters Pub Brewery downtown and Corner Brew Pub in Sugar House. I will not even start with the construction debacle that has destroyed many businesses in Sugar House, and we have been struggling to survive. But why would are government proactively discourage people from visiting businesses downtown by making it more expensive to park downtown. You have already started by eliminating driving lanes to create more for bikes and buses. You act as if Salt Lake City has a proper public transportation system, but it does not. You make policy as if we do not have a winter or extremely hot summers. Do you believe that people will ride bikes to downtown and in downtown year-round. When is the last time you have ridden a bike to work, taken a bus or Trax to a restaurant downtown? For our downtown to survive and thrive, we need to bring people in from outside of downtown proper. I understand the need to raise rates a small amount, but why are you wanting to punish the local citizen for wanting to come downtown and support downtown businesses. You have already increased taxes to support a billionaire who had planned to move the Jazz and the Mammoth down to Sandy. And now you want to punish people who have to drive into downtown? Explain how to get a family of four from Millcreek or any East side location to downtown in a reasonable amount of time without driving? And now the mayor wants them to pay more to the city to come down and support local businesses. Park City, where we have two restaurants, has done their best to keep people from Salt Lake to drive up and support their businesses by making parking too expensive. Salt Lake would be better served by getting more people downtown, spending money at local businesses rather than punishing people who need to drive into downtown. I strongly encourage you to not support this part of the budget. Sincerely, Rick Seven, Salt Lake Brewing Co.

subject: FY25/26 Budget
comment: City Council Members — I want to thank you for your continued and visible support for arts and culture in our capital city. I'm sure you're aware of how the state and federal funding for all kinds of public programs are either in flux or already determined, which will no doubt influence your budget decision-making. Both federal and state funding has been reduced, in some cases drastically, for our arts community. I fully support Mayor Mendenhall's proposed budget for the Salt Lake City Arts Council. I'm asking you to consider making an emergency appropriation for the City Arts Grants program, managed by the City Arts Council, that will help our artists and arts groups get through this time of significant challenges to their operations. If now is not the right time to consider this, you could reconsider the possibility during a budget opening later in the year. Our Capital City is the home for most of the artists and arts and cultural organizations in the state. They live here and work here - contributing as you know to every aspect of our lives. And the City Arts Council's grant program is an existing and effective vehicle to provide emergency support. Thanks for your consideration, Nancy Boskoff, resident District Three

subject: Comment
comment: Dear Salt Lake City Council, It has come to my attention that my previous communication, which I intended as a formal request for an investigation, was apparently categorized merely as a "comment." I must admit, this interpretation is... enlightening, though not particularly encouraging regarding your commitment to addressing constituent concerns seriously. To be perfectly clear, it was not a casual observation; it was a request for you to look into a significant matter. Perhaps my expectation that it would be treated with due diligence was misplaced. For your information, and to underscore the unsuitability of recent treatment by the Salt Lake City Police Department, I am no longer a felon in Salt Lake City and have maintained a clean record for over two decades. The conduct I've experienced from the SLCPD is, frankly, uncalled for and unacceptable. However, if addressing such issues of citizen treatment by law enforcement is not a priority, then so be it. I will, therefore, pivot to a different, perhaps simpler, inquiry. I would like a direct answer to the following question: Is Salt Lake City a sanctuary city? I trust this straightforward question will elicit an equally straightforward response. I will be awaiting your reply. Sincerely, Gary Vogt
